title: Premium curated DAST rule
description: The standard for an enhanced dynamic check in Git Code Review. A rule is data, not code: a fixed engine reads this spec and runs it. A rule is for scanning only the company's own hosted assets, is never destructive, and only reports a weakness that is proven and has an impact. Any tool or model that writes a rule must produce a document that validates against this schema; the server then applies extra safety rules this schema cannot express (listed in each field's notes).

id.description: A short unique slug, lower case with single dashes. Start it with the class, for example injection-php-cgi-arg.

class.description: The area the rule belongs to.

safety.description: read: only GET, HEAD or OPTIONS, changes nothing. neutral: a request that changes nothing lasting (for example a failed login for a user that does not exist). oob: proves the server can be made to make a request, through a callback this product runs, and nothing more.

severity_floor.description: The lowest severity a confirmed finding gets. The engine may raise it on the evidence (for example when a response holds another person's data).

summary.description: Plain language: what weakness this finds and why it matters.

anonymous.description: Send every request without the scan's session.  Use it for any rule about what somebody who is not signed in can see.

needs.description: What the rule needs to run. A rule whose needs are not met is skipped and says so. An oob rule must list oob.

neutral_justification.description: Required by the server when a neutral rule sends POST: one sentence on why the request changes nothing lasting.

probe.description: The requests to send, in order. The engine fills placeholders in braces, such as {route}, {oob} or a saved value.

method.description: PUT, DELETE and PATCH are never allowed and are not listed. A read rule may use only GET, HEAD or OPTIONS (the server enforces this).

path.description: A path on the in-scope host, may contain placeholders.

query.description: Query parameters as name to value.

body.description: A request body for POST. Must change nothing lasting.

oob_token.description: Mints a unique callback token for this step, bound into the request through the {oob} placeholder. Required for an oob rule.

save_as.description: Save part of the response under this name for a later step or the confirm rule.

confirm.description: How a real finding is told from nothing. A bare 200 is never a finding.

control.description: The request that cannot succeed (for example a path that cannot exist), so the normal answer is known. Required for read and neutral rules.

differential.description: The difference the finding stands on, as an expression the engine understands, for example: status==200 and body_differs(control); or oob_hit==true; or timing_differs.

retest.description: How many times the confirming condition is reproduced, so a fluke is not a finding.

max_delay_seconds.description: For a timing oracle only. A probe may wait at most 5 seconds; anything longer is a denial of service and is refused.

reproduce.description: How a security admin repeats the result by hand, for example a curl command. This is what makes a finding fact based rather than a claim.

references.description: Links that back the rule up (OWASP, a vendor advisory, research).

$comment: Extra rules the server enforces beyond this schema: a read rule may use only GET, HEAD or OPTIONS; PUT, DELETE and PATCH are never allowed; a neutral POST needs neutral_justification; an oob rule needs a probe step with an oob_token and oob in needs; no field anywhere may contain a destructive payload (DROP TABLE, DELETE FROM, rm -rf, shutdown, a long sleep, and so on); and every target host must be one of the company's own domains from Settings, or a subdomain under one, or the scan is refused.
